title: Cross-border labor enforcement can produce a reported remedy without proving durable worker power
source_unit: U.S. Trade Representative official resolution announcement for a USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism matter at ThyssenKrupp Springs & Stabilizers de México
geography: San Luis Potosí, Mexico; U.S.-Mexico USMCA labor enforcement and facility response

denominator.unit: named USMCA Rapid Response Labor Mechanism matter at one facility

petition_date.unit: date the interagency committee received the petition

us_review_request_date.unit: date USTR submitted a request to Mexico

workers_reinstated.unit: workers reinstated under former terms and conditions

backpay_and_benefits.unit: backpay and benefits for the two reinstated workers

facility_remediation.value: union access protocol, neutrality and collective-bargaining rules, zero-tolerance policy, and personnel training

mexican_monitoring.value: in-person training and monitoring throughout the review period

trade_response.value: U.S. resumed liquidation of unliquidated entries from the facility

durable_worker_outcome.unit: later receipt verification, non-retaliation, bargaining power, safety, and recurrence

observations.method: Review of USTR's official resolution announcement, which reports the petition, intergovernmental review, facility actions, Mexican monitoring, and tariff-liquidation decision; no independent worker-level follow-up is included.
observations.uncertainty: The announcement is an official enforcement account and does not independently verify payment receipt, whether all affected workers were remedied, the later operation of the union-access protocol, recurrence of retaliation, or durable facility compliance. One case cannot estimate USMCA-wide performance.
observations.subgroup: Two reinstated workers, the named ThyssenKrupp facility, La Liga Sindical Obrera Mexicana, Mexican government monitors, and U.S. trade/labor enforcement institutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: A formal resolution and resumed tariff liquidation can coexist with real improvement, but agency closure does not prove durable worker power. The result may reflect facility-specific negotiation and monitoring rather than a general cross-border labor mechanism effect.

related_sources.claim: Official USTR facility-specific RRM index lists the ThyssenKrupp review, March 16, 2026 resolution, and resumption-of-liquidation letter, with no later ThyssenKrupp-specific follow-up listed at the 2026-10-19 recheck.

boundary: This record measures one official USMCA labor-enforcement case and its reported institutional response. It does not establish worker receipt, durable bargaining power, non-retaliation, sector-wide compliance, causal leverage, or general performance of the Rapid Response Labor Mechanism.

reproduction_audit.result: The USTR facility-specific index lists the March 16, 2026 resolution and resumption-of-liquidation letter as the latest ThyssenKrupp-specific public items; no later facility-specific monitoring, payment, worker, or recurrence record was listed at recheck.
reproduction_audit.interpretation: This is a public-observation cutoff, not evidence that later compliance, worker experience, or durability did not occur.
